brief: Third instance of the class one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument, together with P7's record_row.py HTTP 500: an audit-class barrier. adopt as an audit-class barrier in new fly-in R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY (S, lane F, priority HIGH: it sits on the merge path), in two PRs ordered by file overlap. Do not fold into R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN, which is unregistered and a much larger mechanisation. (1) Third instance of the class "one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument", measured. Across every train log since 2026-10-20 there are 11 TRAIN STOPPED lines, and 2 are transient reads: train 8's `approve: ... could not read pull request #2547` (train2547/state8, 21:50:38Z, after waiting t+2667 s for CI, with 7 entries released) and `ci: the head commit at <sha> could not be read: Get "https://api.github.com/...": net/http...` in merge_train.py's own read. Add P7's record_row.py `HTTP Error 500` on main's push run, whose revisit trigger ("a second 5xx instance") is now met. The remaining 9 stops are content refusals (red CI 3, HOLDER worktree 4, stale carry 1, ledger merge 1), so 18% of train stops are pure transport. (2) The cause and the precedent. app_approve.sh l.104 `js=$(gh api "repos/$1/pulls/$2") || die` has three sibling reads (l.271 comments, l.406 CODEOWNERS, l.408 files), all single-shot, discarding stderr so the failure class is lost. app_push.sh already holds the house pattern (l.188-251: bounded RB_SLEEP*3^(n-1), 5/15/45 s, transport refusals distinguished from a genuine refusal, never retry-forever). Reuse that rule rather than inventing 10/30/60. (3) Classification, so it cannot mask a refusal. Retry only network/transport errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429 or a secondary-rate-limit 403 (honouring Retry-After). Anything else (401, 403-permission, 404, 422, or a body that parses but is wrong: head moved, no verdict, owned path) refuses at once, as today. After the budget it refuses with the last error text kept. Mutation-write calls (review POST, merge) are never retried by this rule; they keep their own guarded paths. (4) Ordering. PR 1, app_approve.sh's four reads plus self-test arms: no open PR or live handoff touches tools/pr/app_approve.sh, so dispatch now, ahead of R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT (P17, same file), which gains an after-edge on it. PR 2, merge_train.py's GitHub reads and record_row.py's urlopen: after #2585 (CI-LAYOUT-P1: merge_train.py, record_row.py), #2584 (MAIN-GATE: merge_train.py) and #2524 (PUSHER-REAP: merge_train.py). Cost: ~25 lines in bash, ~20 in python, one shared rule stated once in INSTRUMENTS.md. Benefit: about 45 min of CI wait plus a relaunch for each transient stop (2 in about 30 h of trains), and one red main push run per 5xx. (5) Null control, in each self-test: a stub `gh` failing once with a transport error then answering passes, with exactly 2 calls logged. A stub answering 404, or a head mismatch, refuses after exactly 1 call (no retry masks a refusal). A stub failing 4 times refuses after the budget, naming the last error. A stub answering 500 to record_row twice then 200 records. Brief addition: "bounded retry of GitHub READS only, app_push.sh's 5/15/45 s rule, retrying transport errors, 5xx, 429 and secondary-limit 403 and nothing else; fixtures: one transient then success (2 calls), 404 and a wrong head (1 call, immediate refuse), budget exhausted (refuse with the last error); PR 1 is app_approve.sh, PR 2 is merge_train.py and record_row.py after #2585, #2584 and #2524".
